Front: What is the fundamental difference between SFT and DPO?
Back: SFT maximizes likelihood of demonstration tokens (behavioral cloning); DPO maximizes likelihood that preferred responses score higher than rejected under an implicit reward model

Front: What is the DPO loss function?
Back: L_DPO = -E[log sigma(beta*(log pi_theta(y_w|x)/pi_ref(y_w|x) - log pi_theta(y_l|x)/pi_ref(y_l|x)))]

Front: What is beta's role in DPO?
Back: Controls KL penalty strength — how far aligned policy can deviate from reference. Low beta: aggressive optimization (reward hacking risk). High beta: conservative (underutilizes preferences)

Front: What beta values should you use for different DPO tasks?
Back: 0.01-0.05: creative writing/style transfer (aggressive); 0.1-0.2: general chat (standard); 0.3-0.5: medical/legal/financial (conservative, safety-first)

Front: Why can't you do DPO on a base model without SFT?
Back: Base model's generation distribution has minimal overlap with preference data distribution; DPO gradients become noisy when pi_ref assigns near-zero probability to both chosen and rejected

Front: By how much does skipping SFT degrade DPO?
Back: Zephyr showed skipping SFT degrades DPO by 15+ points on MT-Bench

Front: How much compute does DPO save vs RLHF (PPO)?
Back: ~40% less because it eliminates the reward model and value network

Front: What mathematical assumption does DPO's derivation rely on?
Back: The Bradley-Terry preference model — preferences are transitive and determined by a scalar reward difference; breaks when preferences are intransitive

Front: How does IPO improve on DPO's assumptions?
Back: IPO adds regularization to prevent overfitting the Bradley-Terry assumption; uses squared error loss requiring preference by only a margin epsilon, not sigmoid-based

Front: What data does KTO need vs DPO?
Back: KTO needs only binary feedback (thumbs up/down) per response; DPO needs paired preferences (which of two responses is better). KTO reduces annotation cost by ~50%

Front: What is GRPO's key advantage over DPO for math?
Back: GRPO uses verifiable rewards (correctness checking) eliminating human annotation entirely; with binary math rewards, group normalization gives clean signal. DPO needs preference pairs

Front: When does DPO vs PPO vs GRPO win?
Back: DPO: clean paired preferences, single-turn. PPO: complex multi-objective or multi-turn. GRPO: verifiable rewards (math, code). KTO: unpaired binary feedback

Front: How do you build a preference dataset for DPO?
Back: Generate 4-8 responses per prompt from SFT model; annotators rank pairwise; filter for >70% agreement; balance so chosen/rejected aren't trivially distinguishable (e.g., by length)

Front: What is the hybrid annotation approach for DPO?
Back: 20% human-annotated (high quality, diverse) + 80% synthetic (scalable, consistent); West-of-N generates synthetic by pairing best-vs-worst of N samples

Front: How does LoRA interact with DPO's reference model?
Back: With LoRA, the base model IS the reference (no separate model needed); log-ratio reduces to logit difference from the adapter, halving memory and eliminating synchronization

Front: What LoRA rank is recommended for DPO vs SFT?
Back: DPO: rank 64-128 (preference learning needs more capacity); SFT: typical rank 16-32

Front: How do you detect reward hacking in DPO?
Back: Monitor gap between implicit reward (DPO log-ratio) and actual human win-rate; if implicit reward rises while win-rate plateaus or drops, model is hacking patterns

Front: What are the four detection signals for DPO reward hacking?
Back: Length divergence (>30% increase); Diversity collapse (distinct n-gram <0.7); Win-rate saturation (implicit reward climbs, MT-Bench plateaus); Sycophancy (agreement >80%)

Front: How do you prevent catastrophic forgetting during DPO?
Back: Mix 5-15% SFT replay data into DPO batches; use low LR (5e-7); monitor held-out capability benchmarks; use LoRA for isolation (disable adapter if regression)

Front: What is online/iterative DPO and what problem does it solve?
Back: Generates new responses from current policy, collects fresh preferences, trains next iteration — solves distribution shift where policy diverges from static training data

Front: How do you scale DPO to 70B+ parameters?
Back: LoRA for memory (95% saved); ZeRO-3 for weight sharding; gradient checkpointing (60% activation savings, +33% compute); reference offload to CPU or use LoRA-as-reference

Front: What is the memory requirement for full-parameter DPO on 70B?
Back: ~700GB minimum: policy (140GB) + reference (140GB) + optimizer states (280GB) + gradients (140GB) — exceeds 8xA100-80GB

Front: Can you extract the implicit reward from a DPO-trained model?
Back: Yes: r(x,y) = beta*log(pi_DPO(y|x)/pi_ref(y|x)); valid only where policy has coverage, extrapolates poorly OOD

Front: What is the theoretical relationship between DPO and RLHF?
Back: Mathematically equivalent under Bradley-Terry assumption — DPO implicitly learns the same reward function but parameterizes it through policy log-ratio rather than separate network

Front: When does the DPO-RLHF equivalence break?
Back: Bradley-Terry misspecified (intransitive preferences); policy class restricted (LoRA can't represent optimal policy); optimization imperfect (finite data/training)

Front: What does the sigma(-u) term in DPO gradient do?
Back: Acts as adaptive weight: when model correctly ranks y_w > y_l (u>>0), gradient vanishes; when wrong (u<<0), full gradient applied — analogous to hard-example mining

Front: How should you set beta empirically?
Back: Set beta so initial u-values have mean ~0 and std ~1 across training set; ensures sigma(-u) ~0.5 at start with full dynamic range available

Front: What is the relationship between beta and learning rate in DPO?
Back: Per-sample gradient magnitude proportional to beta*(1-sigma(u)); lower beta amplifies implicit reward gap; product beta*LR should remain roughly constant for stability

Front: What is DPO's noise sensitivity vs PPO?
Back: DPO is MORE sensitive — each pair's gradient directly updates policy (flipped label = wrong direction). PPO's RM averages noise across many pairs before policy update

Front: What inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) is needed for DPO?
Back: kappa > 0.8: safe. 0.6-0.8: filter to majority-agreed pairs only. < 0.6: will actively harm DPO training

Front: What is the "iterative LoRA DPO" pattern?
Back: Merge adapter into base (new reference), generate fresh pairs from merged model, train new LoRA; each iteration allows O(rank) additional movement from original base

Front: What is the production evaluation protocol for DPO models?
Back: Daily: MT-Bench + safety (30 min). Weekly: 200 LLM-panel + 50 human samples. Pre-deploy: 500+ human pairwise comparisons, require >55% win-rate with p<0.05

Front: What is the self-preference bias in LLM-as-Judge evaluation?
Back: Models prefer outputs similar to their own style (+10-15% bias); mitigate with diverse judge panel, position-swap debiasing, and human calibration on 200 samples

Front: What correlation do automated evaluators have with human rankings?
Back: ~0.85 at model-level (good for model selection) but only ~0.65 at instance-level (poor for individual responses)

Front: What is the "killer framing" for SFT vs DPO?
Back: SFT sets the floor (competence); DPO raises the ceiling (preference alignment). Production needs both — SFT alone lacks preference signal, DPO alone lacks behavioral grounding

Front: What are the data volume requirements for SFT vs DPO?
Back: SFT: 10K-100K demonstrations. DPO: 50K-200K preference pairs. KTO: same volume but binary (cheaper to collect)

Front: How does LoRA constrain DPO training?
Back: Bounds policy's deviation from reference to low-rank subspace, acting as implicit KL regularization; limits magnitude of preference-driven changes

Front: What "Staff says" vs "Principal says" about beta?
Back: Staff: "beta=0.1 is the standard." Principal: "beta should be set so initial u-values have unit variance — compute it empirically from the first batch"

Front: What "Staff says" vs "Principal says" about DPO convergence?
Back: Staff: "DPO training converges fast." Principal: "Fast convergence often means reward hacking — track win-rate against held-out human eval, not training loss"

Front: What is the reference model staleness problem in DPO?
Back: pi_ref freezes quality floor at training time while world's expectations evolve; periodically updating pi_ref destabilizes training if done too frequently

Front: What is KTO's loss function concept?
Back: Asymmetric treatment: losses from bad responses loom larger than gains from good (prospect theory); uses binary signal without pairing, centered by E_ref subtraction

Front: What is the GRPO formula for advantages in DPO comparison context?
Back: A_i = (r_i - mean(r_1..G))/std(r_1..G) — uses group-sampled statistics, no value network; works when rewards are verifiable and high-variance

Front: What is West-of-N synthetic preference generation?
Back: Sample N responses per prompt, pair best-vs-worst as chosen/rejected; achieves 90%+ of human-annotation quality for DPO training

Front: How do you prevent iterative DPO from collapsing into "safe" responses?
Back: High generation temperature (0.9-1.0); reject near-identical pairs (edit distance <10%); exploration prompts; monitor policy entropy

Front: What is the debugging step when DPO training loss doesn't decrease?
Back: Check: 1) preference labels correct (sample 20, verify); 2) beta too high (mean sigma(-u) <0.1); 3) LR too low (grad norm <1e-6); 4) wrong reference model loaded

Front: What is the LoRA DPO production recipe for 70B?
Back: LoRA on 8xA100s with DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 (optimizer+gradient sharding), fp16 policy, bf16 frozen base-as-reference; 100K pairs: ~48 GPU-hours

Front: What numerical consistency issue exists with distributed DPO reference models?
Back: fp32 vs fp16 reference logprobs diverge by O(1e-3) per token, compounding over 2048 tokens to O(1.0) total; compute reference logprobs in fp32 even when training in fp16

Front: How does AlpacaFarm validate synthetic preference pipelines?
Back: Showed synthetic eval correlates r=0.97 with human rankings for method development (choosing between DPO variants, tuning beta); validates synthetic for development, human for deployment

Front: What are the monthly costs at enterprise scale for DPO?
Back: ~$205K/month: $50K compute (daily iterations, 70B), $150K annotation (human+synthetic), $5K LLM eval

Front: What is the nuclear rollback protocol for reward hacking?
Back: Immediately rollback to pre-DPO SFT checkpoint (known-safe baseline); SFT model may be less preferred but won't exhibit adversarial exploits
